title: Live Cell Imaging during Mechanical Stretch
protocol: Cut the outline of the flexible membrane from PDMS sheets coated with Collagen I using a scalpel or die.
Place each membrane in a 60 mm Petri dish for storage.
Mix PDMS at a 10:1 weight ratio of elastomer A to elastomer B (curing agent).
Pour 5 ml of fully mixed PDMS into 50 ml tubes.
Place 50 ml tubes with uncured PDMS horizontally in a hybridization oven.
Use the rotor function to coat the inner walls of the tubes at 8 rpm during curing time.
Remove the PDMS from the tube in a sterile cell culture hood after full curing.
Partition the cylinder of PDMS into sections 4 mm in height using a new razor blade.
Place the PDMS sections, which will serve as membrane walls, into a Petri dish container without allowing them to become creased.
Select and center one wall of PDMS on one membrane while maintaining both in the Petri dish.
Gently place uncured PDMS (10:1 ratio) on the outside perimeter of the wall to be used as glue.
Prevent formation of gaps between the wall and the membrane since it is there to retain liquid.
Place each Petri dish containing the completed membrane and covered in an oven at 70 °C for 24 hours to cure.
Start the software controlling the motor.
Displace the clamps using the manual setting in the motor software.
Measure the distance and record the motor count position between opposing clamps at both minimum and maximum displacement.
Calculate the percent change in distance as a function of motor count (~0-75k counts).
Seed MLE12 cells at 2.5 million cells per well on a flexible membrane to be confluent within two days.
Remove cell culture media from the wells.
Punch two holes in each of the six clamp tabs using 1.5 mm biopsy punches.
Position the punched holes to line up with the pins within the clamps for no pre-tension.
Place the membrane on the stretcher and position it so that the punched holes align with the pins.
Place top clamps into place, tightening screws one at a time alternating sides.
Add 1 ml of cell culture media to each well.
Place the device on the microscope stage, centering the middle of the membrane with the light path.
Use tape or magnets to fix the device to the stage.
Control the in-plane movement with the stage controller of the microscope.
Control the vertical (z-direction) movement with the stage controller of the microscope.
Apply stretch manually using the software provided by the manufacturer.
Add 1-2 ml of RT DMEM containing mitochondrial superoxide indicator at a final concentration of 5 µM directly to the cells.
Incubate for 10 min at 37 °C.
Wash cells gently three times with warmed buffer.
Place the flexible membrane on the stretcher under an upright confocal microscope.
Add 1 ml of DMEM with phenol-red free medium and 25 mM HEPES.
Set excitation/emission filters to 510/580 nm.
Image multiple fields every 15 min for a time course of mitochondrial superoxide production.
Record fluorescence intensity histograms at each time interval using appropriate software.
Prepare the AFM for the experiment.
Increase the height of the AFM head to its maximum position in the z-direction.
Extend the legs of the AFM with extenders.
Lift the specimen and AFM head to accommodate the mechanical device height.
Prepare the optical microscope if available.
Remove the AFM scanner plate.
Remove the desired objective lens from the AFM.
Add a spacer to the objective lens.
Mount the objective back in its original location.
Place the scanner plate back onto the AFM.
Start the AFM software.
Activate all necessary light sources, including those for fluorescence measurements.
Mount a chip with an appropriate cantilever beam for the desired measurements.
Align the laser according to manufacturer’s guidelines on a glass coverslip mounted on the device.
Calibrate the cantilever stiffness following the manufacturer's instructions.
Prepare a membrane as per step 1 protocols.
Cut the walls of the membrane to approximately 1 mm in height immediately before mounting onto the stretching device.
Mount the membrane on the mechanical device as described in 3.2.1-3.2.3.
Remove cell culture media from the membrane.
Couple the device with an adapter.
Place the mechanical device and adapter on the scanner.
Stretch the membrane to the desired tensile strain level.
Add a limited volume (<0.5 ml) of media on the cells.
Engage the cantilever beam with the membrane.
Follow the protocol of the particular AFM device to scan areas of interest.
